6. Call `aios_router_record_turn_result` tool with actual read/check facts.
7. Call `aios_router_complete_lane` tool with a nonempty receipt.

After each tool, emit visible `[DRONE SELF-PROMPT]` fields `Agenda:`, `Verified facts:`, `Next bounded action:` grounded in the latest result. Final response starts `[DRONE]`, names the target and function, includes actual PASS output, then ends with the same fields and `Next bounded action: STOP`.

The Architect authorized this bounded LocalCoder task. The Queen fixed the exact tool sequence to: aios_router_open_build_task → aios_router_accept_self_prompt → localcoder_add_python → read → shell → aios_router_record_turn_result → aios_router_complete_lane. OpenCode permission checks and the Rust WSL Docker Body gate remain authoritative.

[QUEEN → DRONE]
Execute only that sequence, in order, one tool at a time. Do not retry a denied or failed tool. After each non-final tool result, emit a visible [DRONE SELF-PROMPT] with exactly these labels on separate lines: Agenda:, Verified facts:, Next bounded action:. Verified facts must cite the latest actual tool evidence, not the path or directory name alone. Name the next assigned tool in Next bounded action. After the final tool, combine the report and self-prompt in one final message: it must start exactly with [DRONE], state the actual target filename and one concrete fact from returned content, then end with [DRONE SELF-PROMPT] and the same fields; Next bounded action must be STOP.
